transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-14 15:30 UTC — Duration 48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood CSM), Arjun (SummitCorp CTO), Sofia (Lead ML Eng), Ben (Infra), Tara (Product)

00:00 Maya: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for hopping on, uh this is the weekly POC sync; we'll focus on the unit econ numbers and the tuning we did last week.
00:12 Arjun: thanks Maya, appreciate it. quick note — we're pretty tight on timeline, execs want a go/no-go decision end of month.
00:20 Maya: understood, so we'll keep this tight. Liam, do you want to run through the updated dashboard numbers?
00:27 Liam: yeah sure, uh quick context: we re-ran the workload with prefix caching enabled for the top 120 prompt traces and bumped the batching window to 6ms in the dynamic batcher. overall throughput improvement and cost shifts are in the deck i shared.
00:40 Sofia: just to clarify, by prefix caching you mean KV cache of encoder/decoder prefixes, right? not the response post-process caching?
00:46 Liam: correct — it's the KV cache warm path so repeated prefix tokens don't re-evaluate attention, we still allow full generative steps.
00:53 Tara: what were the hit rates you saw for the cache? that will determine savings.
00:57 Liam: on our run hit rate averaged 22 to 25% across the three prompt families; highest for the short form prompts (30%) and lowest for long-context support prompts (~12%).
01:08 Ben: and how did that translate to dollars — tokens saved or tokens/$?
01:12 Liam: good question — raw numbers: before caching we measured ~18,400 tokens per $1 (this is model variant small-6b on our infra profile). after caching and 6ms batching we moved to ~24,000 tokens per $1 — so roughly a 30% tokens-per-dollar improvement.
01:27 Arjun: 30% is decent, but we care about latency for our UI. how did p95/p99 change with 6ms batching?
01:33 Liam: median latency stayed similar, p95 increased by about 30ms on average and p99 had some spikes up to 220ms in a couple of bursts. the dynamic batcher will wait up to the window or until batch fullness, so there's a tail tradeoff.
01:47 Sofia: 220ms p99 might be too high for our live chat flows — our SLO is 300ms end-to-end but that includes network and client-side. we prefer model infer p99 under 200ms ideally.
01:58 Liam: we can tune the batching policy — smaller max window or prioritize latency-sensitive routes with no batching, and route longer async requests to the batched path. that's actually one of Redwood's smart-routing configs.
02:09 Maya: yes, route-based policies — you can set latency SLO per route and the router will favor lower-latency backends or smaller batchers. that will raise cost a bit for those requests but you keep UX.
02:19 Arjun: can you quantify the cost delta if we set chat route to minimal batching?
02:23 Liam: approximate: if you exclude the chat route (which is about 35% of volume) from batching you lose about 11–13% of overall tokens/$ efficiency. so tokens/$ would drop from 24k to roughly 21k.
02:35 Tara: hmm ok, that might be acceptable. what about quantization — you mentioned a q4 model variant earlier?
02:41 Liam: yes we ran q4_0 quantization on the 6b and saw about 18% cost reduction versus fp16 on the same hardware with negligible quality delta for the prompts you provided. that stacks with caching. so combined caching + quant we saw a ~45% reduction from the original baseline.
02:56 Ben: any implications for KPIs like CPU/GPU utilization or memory pressure?
03:01 Liam: q4 lowers memory footprint so you get more concurrency per GPU. batching increases GPU utilization (good for $/token) but also increases per-request latency; caching reduces compute per request so it lowers utilization. it's a balancing act.
03:15 Sofia: were there any mismatches in the A/B quality tests? some of our prompts are sensitive to tokenization differences.
03:21 Liam: we did a small eval set — 1200 requests — automated metric delta was within tolerance but we flagged 18 cases for human review; mostly edge contexts where the model used slightly different phrasing. we'll share the eval report.
03:34 Arjun: can you run a longer run with our traffic mix? last time the live skew caused more misses in cache than you predicted.
03:40 Maya: absolutely — we propose a 24-hour ramped throughput benchmark with Sofia's prompt families and real traffic mix. Liam will include a warmed KV cache path and cold-warm transitions to measure steady-state vs warmup.
03:52 Liam: yep i can do that — i'll also capture per-route tokens/sec/$ and latency percentiles. planning to run on the dedicated trial pool so numbers are representative.
04:02 Sofia: timeline? we need results before 02/22 ideally.
04:06 Liam: i'll aim to have the harness run and initial numbers by 02/21.
04:09 Maya: on the security angle — Arjun asked for SOC 2, SSO, KMS details last week — i've got that pack ready to send.
04:16 Arjun: yep important. also we want to know about Private deployment network egress limits — Ben will share that doc.
04:22 Ben: i'll send the VPC egress constraints and our KMS provider config.
04:25 Tara: pricing — can you send a quick hosted vs dedicated comparison with burst capacity?
04:30 Maya: yes i'll include three scenarios: conserved-hosted (lower ops, higher per-token), dedicated-reserved (committed monthly with lower per-token), and dedicated-with-burst (reserved baseline + hourly burst pricing). i'll price them with the observed q4+cache numbers and also with conservative no-cache case.
04:44 Arjun: one question on fallback — if dedicated pool is saturated do you support auto-fallback to a cheaper hosted variant?
04:50 Liam: yes, Redwood's routing supports fallback tiers; you can define policies: first try dedicated, then hosted reduced-size model, then a lower-cost region or last resort. fallbacks can be configured to preserve quality or preserve latency.
05:03 Sofia: okay good — helps with our availability story.
05:06 Maya: recap on actions: liam run 24h benchmark; sofia upload prompt sets; maya send pricing + security pack; ben send infra constraints. we'll meet same time next week to review numbers and decide if we push for dedicated pilot.
05:18 Arjun: sounds good, thanks everyone.
05:21 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the deck and the benchmark plan.
05:26 (call ends)
